```{r options, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", error = FALSE)
```

biocroxytest is for developers of R packages. Write testthat checks beside
an R function, then let roxygen2 generate ordinary test files. You keep
using testthat to run the tests. You can add a separate Bioconductor long-test
suite later.

This tutorial starts with a prepared package, so you can try the workflow
without configuring your own project. It uses the **GitHub development
version** of biocroxytest; the Bioconductor release has a separate
[release guide](https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/biocroxytest/inst/doc/biocroxytest.html).

## Install the tutorial dependencies

Run this once in R. Use R 4.4 or newer and a compatible Bioconductor release.
The optional HDF5 dependency is used in the next tutorial.

```{r installation, eval=FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("remotes")
BiocManager::install(c("SummarizedExperiment", "HDF5Array", "testthat"), update = FALSE)
BiocManager::install("xec-cm/biocroxytest@devel", update = FALSE)
```

## Copy the example package

Run the following blocks in order in an R session. All operations use `pkg`
explicitly, so you do not need to change the working directory. The copy lives
in a temporary directory and can be discarded after the tutorial.

```{r copy-package}
template <- system.file("examples", "samplealignment", package = "biocroxytest",
                        mustWork = TRUE)
pkg <- tempfile("samplealignment-")
fs::dir_copy(template, pkg)
```

The important files in the copy are:

```text
samplealignment/
  DESCRIPTION                 Package dependencies and roxygen configuration
  R/align-samples.R            Function and its test declaration
  R/example-experiment.R      Three samples with known measurements
  tests/testthat.R             Standard testthat runner
```

You can also inspect the [complete example package on GitHub](https://github.com/xec-cm/biocroxytest/tree/devel/inst/examples/samplealignment).
To keep your work, use a new persistent directory instead of `tempfile()`.

## Read the function and its test

Our function selects samples from a `SummarizedExperiment`. Asking for `s3`
and then `s1` must return both measurements and metadata in that order.
The input contains one gene:

| Sample | Count | Condition |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| s1 | 11 | control |
| s2 | 21 | control |
| s3 | 31 | treated |

Open `R/align-samples.R` in the copy. Its complete contents are:

```{r first-source, code=readLines(file.path(pkg, "R", "align-samples.R")), eval=FALSE}
```

`example_experiment()` constructs the small object above. The three
`expect_identical()` calls check sample order, counts and conditions against
explicit expected values. `@tests` tells biocroxytest to put these checks in
an ordinary test. A **roclet** is the roxygen2 extension that does that writing.

## Generate the test

The example's `DESCRIPTION` already contains this configuration:

```text
Roxygen: list(roclets = c("namespace", "rd", "biocroxytest::tests_roclet"))
```

The bundled package is already configured. Generate its test and refresh
the function documentation together:

```{r generate, message=FALSE}
roxygen2::roxygenise(pkg)
```

The test is written to
`tests/testthat/test-roxytest-tests-align-samples.R`. It is an ordinary
testthat file; the `roxytest` filename prefix preserves compatibility with
existing test and snapshot paths.

```{r generated-source, code=readLines(file.path(pkg, "tests", "testthat", "test-roxytest-tests-align-samples.R")), eval=FALSE}
```

Edit the declaration in `R/align-samples.R` and regenerate when changing
the test. Commit the generated file alongside the source.

## Run it and read the result

```{r first-run, message=FALSE}
result <- testthat::test_local(pkg, reporter = "silent")
as.data.frame(result)[c("failed", "error", "passed")]
```

There should be **three passing expectations, zero failures and no error**.
For interactive progress, omit `reporter = "silent"`. In your own package,
`devtools::test()` from its root runs the ordinary suite too.

```{r verify-first-run, include=FALSE}
summary <- as.data.frame(result)
stopifnot(sum(summary$passed) == 3L, sum(summary$failed) == 0L, !any(summary$error))
```

## See the test catch a bug

A tempting implementation uses `%in%` to select matching columns. It finds
the correct samples but retains their original order, returning `s1, s3`.
Change the function's final line to the following. This R block performs
the edit for you:

```{r introduce-bug}
source_file <- file.path(pkg, "R", "align-samples.R")
correct <- readLines(source_file)
broken <- correct
broken[startsWith(broken, "align_samples <-")] <-
  "align_samples <- function(x, samples) x[, colnames(x) %in% samples]"
writeLines(broken, source_file)
```

The assertions have not changed, so their generated file is still current.
Run them again, keeping the result so we can inspect the expected failure:

```{r catch-bug, message=FALSE}
result <- testthat::test_local(pkg, reporter = "silent", stop_on_failure = FALSE)
as.data.frame(result)[c("failed", "error", "passed")]
```

All three expectations now fail: the order is reversed, along with the
counts and conditions. `stop_on_failure = FALSE` is useful for this deliberate
failure; normally keep the default so test failures stop the check.

```{r verify-bug, include=FALSE}
summary <- as.data.frame(result)
stopifnot(sum(summary$failed) == 3L, !any(summary$error))
```

Restore the correct function and require a passing run:

```{r restore, message=FALSE}
writeLines(correct, source_file)
result <- testthat::test_local(pkg, reporter = "silent")
as.data.frame(result)[c("failed", "error", "passed")]
```

## Apply this to your own package

From your package root, set up ordinary tests with `usethis::use_testthat()`
(install usethis first if needed). Add the roclet above to the existing
`Roxygen` configuration, retaining any other settings. Add `@tests` beside a
function, regenerate, and run `devtools::test()`.

Declare test dependencies in `Suggests`. Install biocroxytest wherever you
regenerate tests; the generated ordinary tests do not need it at runtime.
For package checks, build the source and pass the resulting tarball to the
check command, for example in a terminal:

```sh
R CMD build samplealignment
R CMD check --no-manual samplealignment_0.0.1.tar.gz
```

Here `samplealignment` is a persistent copy of the example package in your
terminal's working directory. Substitute your own directory and package version.

**Next:** [share the same checks between memory and HDF5](named-cases.html).
The next tutorial starts with a fresh copy, so you can also follow it independently.

```{r cleanup, include=FALSE}
pkgload::unload("samplealignment")
unlink(pkg, recursive = TRUE)
```
